cards.front: Series RLC natural frequency and damping
cards.back: ω₀=1/√(LC), α=R/(2L), ζ=α/ω₀. ζ<1 is underdamped; ζ=1 is critically damped; ζ>1 is overdamped.
E_C=½CV² and E_L=½LI² exchange in the reactive elements; a positive R dissipates energy and damps the unforced transient.
At ω₀, XL=XC and Z=R; for a series RLC, Q=ω₀L/R=1/(2ζ). Positive resistance keeps resonant current finite.
Below resonance XL−XC<0 and current leads; above resonance XL−XC>0 and current lags. Check phase using the chosen source and current references.
V_out = −R_f Σ V_k/R_k; the virtual ground isolates the inputs, so each contributes independently (superposition).
V_out = −(1/RC)∫V_in dt; with no DC path an offset ramps it to saturation, so a parallel R_f bounds the DC gain to −R_f/R above a corner 1/(2πR_fC).
V_out = −RC dV_in/dt; gain 2πfRC rises with frequency and amplifies noise, so a series input resistor caps it.
Inverting low-pass: DC gain −R_f/R_in, corner 1/(2πR_fC_f). Unity-gain Sallen–Key (equal R): f₀ = 1/(2πR√(C₁C₂)), Q = ½√(C₁/C₂). Bandwidth ≈ GBW/noise gain.

cards.front: When does a loading factor belong in the gain chain?
cards.back: When the input is an open-circuit source voltage. A voltage already specified at the amplifier terminals must not be loaded a second time.

cards.front: Does 80 dB CMRR mean 80% common-mode removal?
cards.back: No. CMRR in decibels is 20 log10(A_d/A_cm). Convert the amplitude-gain ratio before computing an output error.

cards.front: Why is a Nyquist threshold alone an incomplete acquisition design?
cards.back: It does not state transition-band attenuation, out-of-band signal/noise levels, phase at the exact boundary or acquisition settling.

cards.front: What is the reference point of an input-referred ADC step?
cards.back: It is the stated input node obtained by dividing the output code step by the gain from that node. Include loading only when referring farther back to an open-circuit source.

cards.front: What makes a signal-path report reproducible?
cards.back: Label the voltage basis at each node, give equations and units, distinguish supplied inputs from inferred quantities, and name the physical specifications the model lacks.

cards.front: What defines the nonlinear bias point?
cards.back: A simultaneous solution of the device law and the original network constraints, followed by a domain and residual check.

cards.front: Why is V/I not generally the small-signal resistance?
cards.back: The local slope dV/dI and the secant V/I coincide for a through-origin linear resistor but differ for a nonlinear law.

cards.front: Which balance checks the solved load line?
cards.back: Source supplied power equals resistor plus device absorbed power under the declared references; voltage ratios alone do not close the ledger.

cards.front: What does a successful root solver establish?
cards.back: It establishes a solution of the supplied equations within numerical error, not the empirical validity or universal range of those equations.

cards.front: Why check a region after computing a transistor current?
cards.back: A piecewise law is conditional. A calculated candidate is usable only when its voltage/current inequalities and the network equation all hold.

cards.front: What constrains a small-signal amplifier claim?
cards.back: The solved bias, device derivative, network loading, perturbation size and preservation of the assumed operating region.

cards.front: How should multiple algebraic roots be interpreted?
cards.back: Substitute each into the original equations and region inequalities; a polynomial root outside the assumed branch is not an operating point on that branch.

cards.front: Which idealizations must accompany a MOS bias report?
cards.back: The exact kappa convention, threshold, region law, zero channel-length modulation and gate-current assumption, plus the effects those choices omit.

cards.front: Why calculate a characteristic equation after DC gain?
cards.back: The equilibrium value and the decay or growth of deviations answer separate questions.

cards.front: What establishes asymptotic stability of this finite linear model?
cards.back: Every closed-loop eigenvalue has a strictly negative real part; a negative feedback label alone does not establish it.

cards.front: Can stable open-loop poles become unstable after feedback?
cards.back: Yes. The closed-loop characteristic equation changes; phase and pole structure matter even with a negative feedback connection.

cards.front: Why cannot an equal-pole threshold be copied to a compensated circuit?
cards.back: Changing the pole distribution or feedback changes the characteristic equation and the applicable stability conditions.

cards.front: What should a nonlinear port report retain?
cards.back: The supplied law and load line, admissible interval, numerical residual, derivative, refinement and independent power balance.

cards.front: How do sensitivity and conservation complement a root residual?
cards.back: Sensitivity tests local response and conservation closes another original equation; neither establishes that a synthetic law fits a real component.

cards.front: What checks distinguish a valid small-signal calculation?
cards.back: Verify the nonlinear bias first, then differentiate that branch and the original network, with finite perturbations checked separately.

cards.front: What must accompany a piecewise algebraic solution?
cards.back: Original-equation substitution and every region inequality, including the rejected candidates and reason for rejection.

cards.front: How can a feedback report verify more than a static gain?
cards.back: Derive characteristic roots and a compatible state model, check equilibrium and initial slopes, then compare integration under refinement.

cards.front: When should a simulated operating claim stop?
cards.back: At the declared model/range boundary, with unstable modes, numerical error and missing nonlinear mechanisms reported separately.

cards.front: Which assumptions make the two-stage noise calculation valid?
cards.back: Declared one-sided density, squared magnitude, flat mathematical input spectrum, unity DC gain and ideal buffering; actual bandwidth/loading need evidence.

cards.front: Why can full common-noise cancellation fail to minimize total variance?
cards.back: The reference channel adds its own independent noise. The optimum balances that contribution against the shared component under a justified covariance model.
